title: Describe the architecture of my project
prompt:
# Story: Describe the architecture of my project, and have every story checked against it

- **Story**: XXX-architecture-description
- **Created**: 2026-11-05
- **Status**: Draft

## Story

As a team member, I want one screen where I write the architecture of my system (its style, its layers and the rules between them),
improve it with AI if I want, and keep it in the repository, so that every story I write in the Builder is checked against those
layers and each rule is placed in the right one.

---

# The use cases

What a team member does with the Architecture screen, and what happens in the rest of the product.

| # | The user... | What they see | Where it is tested |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | chooses "Architecture" in the menu | the page with an empty box, "Empty. That is allowed.", and a Sync button | The screen |
| 2 | writes the style, the layers and the dependency rules | "Unsaved changes.", a Save button and "Discard changes" | Writing and saving |
| 3 | presses Save | "Saved." and the button says "Saved" for a moment | Writing and saving |
| 4 | changes their mind and presses "Discard changes" | the box goes back to the saved text | Writing and saving |
| 5 | presses "Improve with AI", then "Clarify the layers", reads the proposal and presses "Use this text" | a comment and a "Proposed text" card; the box changes, nothing is saved yet | Improve with AI |
| 6 | presses Save, then Sync | a pull request with `architecture.md` | The repository on GitHub |
| 7 | (a colleague changes `architecture.md` on GitHub) comes back to the page | the box shows the new text, and a notice says it was updated | The repository on GitHub |
| 8 | goes to the Builder and asks for a story | the text goes to the model with the story's prompt; the story names the layer of each rule | Where the architecture is used |
| 9 | asks for a diagram or a UI example of the story | the same text goes with that request | Where the architecture is used |

## The screen

```
Architecture
The architecture of the system: its style, its layers and the rules between them. Stories are checked against it.

(i) This description goes with the prompts of a story, so that ...                              [ Sync ]
    It is kept in the repository as architecture.md when you press Sync.

+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Describe the architecture: the style (for example a modular monolith), the layers and     |
| what each one is responsible for, which layer may depend on which, and the modules.      |
| You can leave it empty.                                              16 rows, resizable  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Unsaved changes.                                          [ Discard changes ]   [ (v) Save ]

[ Improve with AI ]      (opens the panel: four quick actions, a free text box, the replies)
```

---

# Acceptance tests

The screen

- [ ] **Given** a project, **When** the user chooses "Architecture" in the menu, **Then** the page is titled "Architecture" with the
  description "The architecture of the system: its style, its layers and the rules between them. Stories are checked against it."
- [ ] **Given** the page, **Then** a blue note shows: "This description goes with the prompts of a story, so that the story is checked
  against the layers and each rule is placed in the right one. It is not sent with enablers, drivers or ADRs. It is kept in the
  repository as architecture.md when you press Sync." and a Sync button sits on its right.
- [ ] **Given** the page, **Then** one box of 16 rows that can be resized in height shows the text, with the accessible name "The
  architecture of <project name>" and the placeholder "Describe the architecture: the style (for example a modular monolith), the
  layers and what each one is responsible for, which layer may depend on which, and the modules. You can leave it empty."
- [ ] **Given** the page, **Then** it can be read and written with no model connected and no repository connected.

Writing and saving

- [ ] **Given** a project that never had an architecture, **Then** the box is empty, "Empty. That is allowed." shows under it, "Save" is
  disabled and there is no "Discard changes".
- [ ] **Given** the box, **When** the user changes the text, **Then** "Unsaved changes." shows in amber, "Save" is enabled and "Discard
  changes" shows.
- [ ] **Given** unsaved changes, **When** the user presses Save, **Then** the text is saved as typed, "Saved." shows, the button reads
  "Saved" for about two and a half seconds and is disabled, and "Discard changes" goes away.
- [ ] **Given** unsaved changes, **When** the user presses "Discard changes", **Then** the box shows the saved text again and nothing
  else changes.
- [ ] **Given** the box has the focus, **When** the user presses Enter, **Then** a new line is added. The text is saved only with the
  Save button.
- [ ] **Given** a saved text, **When** the user clears the box and saves, **Then** it is saved empty and "Empty. That is allowed."
  shows.
- [ ] **Given** a saved text, **When** the page is reloaded, **Then** the same text shows, with its line breaks and spaces as they were
  typed.
- [ ] **Given** two projects, **Then** each shows its own architecture.

Improve with AI

- [ ] **Given** the page, **Then** an "Improve with AI" button shows under the Save row. **When** it is pressed, **Then** a panel opens
  with the same title, a button "Hide the assistant", four quick actions ("Improve this", "Clarify the layers", "Add dependency rules",
  "Ask me questions"), a text box ("Ask for a change, for example: focus on security") and a Send button, disabled while the box is
  empty.
- [ ] **Given** the panel, **When** the user presses a quick action, or types a request and presses Enter or Send, **Then** the request
  shows as a bubble on the right, and the reply is written on the left as it arrives. Enter does not save the page.
- [ ] **Given** a request, **Then** the model receives the text that is in the box now, saved or not ("(empty)" when there is none), and
  the instruction. It also receives, as context, the project name and the ADRs, and nothing else: no drivers, stories, enablers,
  principles or practices.
- [ ] **Given** a reply, **Then** it shows a short comment and, when the model proposes a new text, a "Proposed text" card with a
  button "Use this text". **When** the user presses it, **Then** the proposal is in the box, "Unsaved changes." shows, and nothing is
  saved. The button reads "In the editor" and is disabled while the box holds that text.
- [ ] **Given** "Ask me questions", **Then** the reply holds questions (up to three) and no proposed text.
- [ ] **Given** a reply that was cut by the length limit, **Then** the card shows "Incomplete, so it cannot be used." and the button is
  disabled.
- [ ] **Given** a reply is being written, **Then** the quick actions are disabled, a Stop button replaces Send, and **When** the user
  presses it, **Then** what was received stays as an incomplete reply.
- [ ] **Given** a request that fails, **Then** the reason shows in red with a "Retry" button, and the failed request is sent again,
  not repeated in the conversation.
- [ ] **Given** the user hides the panel and opens it again, **Then** the conversation is still there. **When** the user leaves the
  page, **Then** it is gone.
- [ ] **Given** a reply, **Then** the token counts of the last request (input, output, cache read, cache write) show under the panel.

The repository on GitHub

- [ ] **Given** no repository is connected, **Then** the Sync button is disabled, with the hint "Connect GitHub in Integrations first".
- [ ] **Given** unsaved changes, **Then** the Sync button is disabled, with the hint "Save the architecture first". What is uploaded
  is the saved text, never the one in the box.
- [ ] **Given** a saved text, **When** the user presses Sync, **Then** the dialog shows what is compared: one file,
  `architecture.md`, with the other documents left out. ADRs are always checked: new and changed ones come down.
- [ ] **Given** the dialog, **When** the user confirms, **Then** `architecture.md` goes to the repository in one pull request, in
  the base folder of the project, with the text as saved and a new line at its end.
- [ ] **Given** an architecture that is empty, or only spaces, **When** the user syncs, **Then** no file is uploaded.
- [ ] **Given** `architecture.md` changed on the base branch and nothing changed here since the last sync, **When** the page is open
  (or gets the focus), **Then** the new text is downloaded and saved, the box shows it, and a notice says "Updated from <branch> and
  saved" with the file name.
- [ ] **Given** the same, but the box has unsaved changes, **Then** a notice says a newer version is on the base branch and that it
  is downloaded when the user saves or discards. **When** the user does, **Then** it is downloaded.
- [ ] **Given** `architecture.md` changed on the base branch and here, **Then** the Sync button shows an amber dot, a warning says
  "Nothing was changed. Solve it on GitHub, then sync." and nothing is overwritten on either side.
- [ ] **Given** a project is connected to a repository that has `architecture.md` and the project has no text, **Then** the file's
  text is brought in once. **When** the project already has text, **Then** it is left alone, and the two are compared when the user
  syncs.
- [ ] **Given** a saved architecture that the user clears and saves, **When** the user syncs, **Then** `architecture.md` stays in the
  repository: deleting a file is not synchronised.

Where the architecture is used

- [ ] **Given** a saved architecture, **When** the user asks the Builder to create a story, edit a story, draw a diagram of a story, or
  make a UI example of a story, **Then** the request carries the section "Architecture of the system (the layers a story must
  respect)" with the text, without the spaces around it.
- [ ] **Given** an empty architecture, **Then** that section is left out of those requests.
- [ ] **Given** the user has unsaved text on this page, **Then** the Builder sends the saved text.
- [ ] **Given** a request about an architectural enabler, **Then** the architecture is not sent. It is not sent either by the driver
  assistant, the principles assistant, or the ADR assistant.
- [ ] **Given** a story requested with an architecture, **Then** the model is told to check the story against it: each rule belongs
  in the right layer, no rule may break a dependency between layers, the layer is named when it helps and cited as "(Architecture)",
  and a part of the request that does not fit the layers is left out and named under Out of scope.
- [ ] **Given** a diagram requested with an architecture, **Then** the model is told to put each container or class in the layer it
  belongs to, and to draw no relationship that breaks a dependency rule.

---

# Business rules and constraints

- The architecture is one document of the project: free text, with no template. It can be empty. Another project never sees it.
- It is written by the team. The AI only proposes: it never changes the box by itself, and nothing is saved until the user presses
  Save.
- It is sent only with what is asked about a story (create, edit, diagram, UI example). It is not part of the context of enablers,
  drivers, ADRs or principles.
- What is saved is what is used: the Builder and the sync read the saved text, not the draft.
- It is kept in the repository as `architecture.md`, with the same rules as every other document: three versions (here, the base
  branch now, and the base branch at the last sync), a pull request for what changed here, a download for what changed there, a
  conflict when both changed, and no deletion.
- The assistant keeps the intent, the language and the facts of the user. It does not invent layers, modules, technologies, names or
  rules: it asks, or leaves a placeholder in square brackets. It writes short statements, with bullets when there are several points,
  and no headings or code fences.
- The assistant is consistent with the ADRs it is given. When the text contradicts an ADR that is Accepted, its comment says so.
- Its comment has at most three sentences, or at most three short questions. A proposal is the whole new text, not a difference.

# Out of scope

- Checking that the text is a good architecture, or that it has layers. Any text is accepted.
- Checking the stories that already exist when the architecture changes, and warning that they may break a rule.
- A history of versions, comparing two versions, and a Markdown preview.
- A structured editor (a list of layers and rules).
- The assistant in general (its panel, the endpoint, the model, the cache): `story-improve-with-ai.md`.
- Connecting GitHub and the sync dialog in general (pull requests, conflicts, the first download): this story only fixes what they
  do for this one file.
- The architecture runway (the diagram of a theme or of the project in the Builder), which is not this document.
- Sending the architecture to the model for enablers, drivers or ADRs.

# Tasks

- [ ] Add "Architecture" to the menu with its icon, title and description.
- [ ] Keep, per project, one free text, empty allowed, saved as typed.
- [ ] Build the page: the note, the Sync button, the box, the status line ("Unsaved changes.", "Saved.", "Empty. That is allowed."), Save
  with its "Saved" moment, and "Discard changes".
- [ ] Show the text that arrives from a download in the box, without losing what the user is typing (the notice and the wait).
- [ ] Add the "Improve with AI" panel with the system prompt, the context (project name and ADRs), the four quick actions, and the
  turn that carries the text in the box and the instruction.
- [ ] Let "Use this text" put a proposal in the box without saving.
- [ ] Write the file `architecture.md` (left out when empty, new line at the end), read it back, and give it its own sync scope: one
  file, ADRs always checked.
- [ ] Block the Sync button while there are unsaved changes, and bring in `architecture.md` when a project connects to a repository
  that has it and the project does not.
- [ ] Add the saved text to the project context of the story requests (create, edit, diagram, UI example), as the section "Architecture
  of the system (the layers a story must respect)", and leave it out for enablers.
- [ ] Add to the story prompt the rule that checks the story against the layers, and to the diagram prompt the rule that places each
  container in its layer.
- [ ] Test with a fake repository: upload, download with and without unsaved changes, conflict, and the first download.

---

## Spike details worth keeping in mind

- The assistant panel is the one made for drivers. Its text box has the accessible name "Ask Claude to change this driver", and the
  turn it builds has "Name: Architecture" and no "Meaning" line (`hint` is empty).
- The assistant gets the ADRs and the text in the box with every request; the text is not in the cached context block, so that the
  block keeps matching the cache while the user edits. The architecture in the Builder's context is the opposite: it is in that block,
  so a change to the text starts a new cache for the Builder.
- The text is saved as typed, with its spaces. Only the check for "empty" (file left out, section left out) ignores spaces.
- The prompt for a UI example does not tell the model what to do with the architecture, although it travels with the request.
- The conversation and the unsaved text live in the page, so they are lost when the user chooses another item of the menu.

## Something to decide

1. **Clearing is local.** When the text is emptied and saved, `buildRepoFiles` leaves the file out and `classify` leaves a file that
   is only missing here alone. `architecture.md` stays on the base branch, and it comes back here if somebody changes it there. If
   clearing should be final, the sync needs a deletion in the pull request (the same rule that a moved story already has).
2. **Unsaved text is lost without a warning** when the user leaves the page, and so is the conversation with the assistant. These tests
   describe what the spike does. Whether to ask before leaving is for the team to decide.
3. **Existing stories are not checked again** when the architecture changes. The architecture reaches a story only when it is
   created, edited or drawn. Whether a changed architecture should flag the stories it affects is a story of its own.
4. **The size of this story.** It holds four things that fit one iteration each: writing and saving (use cases 1 to 4), the AI panel (5),
   the sync (6 and 7), and the use in the Builder (8 and 9). The tests are grouped in that order, so that it can be split as the
   drivers were.
